about: Every mutant was applied to the file as it is at base_commit, which the change that adds this record does not change. killer is the first test nextest reported failing (it stops at the first failure, with tests running in parallel, so another failing test may be reported first on another run). killer_at says where that test function exists: base, or this_commit for a test the change that adds this record adds. A test that exists at base may still kill only through cases that change adds to it: before_this_change gives the verdict at base where it differs. Each mutant that survived its filtered run at base was run again at base against every bridge test (the whole_set run) before it was called a survivor. Every survivor left at this_commit is listed in accepted_survivors with its reason: an equivalent one is marked equivalent, and one that is not says why it is not killed. Every run was on macOS; the file has no code compiled for one platform only. A hand-written mutant's mutation id is the first 32 hex digits of the SHA-256 of its edits in order, each as its from text, a NUL byte, its to text and a NUL byte, in UTF-8. A tool mutant is named as cargo-mutants --list names it, by line and column. Every run was on base_commit, with the file and its test module byte for byte as there (or as this change leaves the test module, for survivors_again).

runs.command: each mutant's edits applied as exact text, then cargo nextest run --locked -p bridge -E 'test(/statement|transfer|pairing|skip|contra|withdraw/)'

as the hand run with every bridge test (-E 'all()'), after the unmutated tree passed all 5092, for the thirty-two hand-written mutants the filtered run missed and the three the tool's run missed. One of them (S097) first failed one test, in a test that reads no statement facts (a Tally runtime read refused while draining); that test passed five runs of five alone on the unmutated tree, and S097 was run again against every test and missed there, which is the verdict recorded
as the whole_set run, for the thirty-five still missed there (thirty-two hand-written, three from the tool)

869:51 replace > with >= in SkipMention:.reason: equivalent: two mentions of one row tie on build time and source id only when they come from one source, and one source mentions a row once. A batch's facts refuse a row id named twice, the journal folds a batch to one entry in one lineage, a lineage keeps one mention per row, and a repeated skip-only record id is refused before its mentions merge. Bridge writes a batch id as bridge- and a version 4 UUID and a skip-only record id as skips- and one (validate_skip_record refuses any other), so neither names the other. A journal holding a batch id of the skip-only form, or a change that lets one source mention a row twice, reopens it

930:65 replace && with || in contra_legs.reason: equivalent, unreachable: an entry's amount reaches contra_legs only through BuildVoucher::of_vouchers, the one place a BuildEntry is made, from the voucher's ImportAmount, and ImportAmount::parse refuses an amount that is zero or carries a sign; both amounts are therefore positive, and the filter passes them whichever way its two conditions are joined. A change that makes a BuildEntry from another source, or lets ImportAmount hold zero or a signed amount, reopens it

S012.reason: equivalent: serde's derive reads an absent field of an Option type as None without #[serde(default)], so the attribute changes nothing a record reads or writes. A change to the field's type, or a deserialize_with on it, reopens it

S013.reason: equivalent, unreachable: the binding of_statement is given comes from bind_ledgers over requested names that include every name the statement uses (ResolvedStatement::ledger_names), each bound by its exact spelling or the build fails (StandardLedgerCatalog::bind_selected); unbindable_masters refuses two requested names that fold equal, case included (twin_fold_keys), but for a pair that differs by a line break, of which only one may be requested. So no binding holds two names equal but for ASCII case, and the search that ignores case finds the exact name. A caller that passes a binding holding two such names reopens it
